scope: C-001 WeChat identity, secure session lifecycle, owner binding and privacy-safe auth transport

T-C001-DB-001.selector: real PostgreSQL identity uniqueness and ciphertext-independent lookup
assertions: concurrent first identity mappings for one provider lookup token commit exactly one account and one ExternalIdentity
the losing account transaction rolls back instead of leaving a half-account fact
ciphertext can change while the provider lookup token continues resolving the same AccountRef

T-C001-CONTRACT-001.selector: closed auth request/session OpenAPI and error contract
assertions: WechatSessionRequest rejects client-supplied owner, openid, unionid and provider fields
SessionView exposes only the opaque session and account-state allowlist, never provider identity or ciphertext fields
login, refresh and rate-limit responses remain on the Accepted stable HTTP/error surface

T-C001-E2E-001.selector: real Nest HTTP WeChat login, refresh, logout, expiry and owner-forgery rejection
assertions: wx code exchange returns a closed session response without openid, unionid, lookup token, ciphertext or accountId
refresh rotates the token and the old token fails closed
expired and revoked sessions fail closed with stable auth errors
upstream rate limiting maps to the stable retryable 429 response
unknown client account_id is rejected before it can become an owner predicate

T-C001-UNIT-001.selector: auth service concurrency, replay, rotation/revoke and synthetic provider failure
assertions: two synthetic wx codes for one subject converge to one account while issuing distinct sessions
the same wx code cannot be replayed
provider failure occurs before persistence and leaves no account/session fact
the synthetic WeChat adapter is forbidden in STAGING, PRODUCTION and RECOVERY
